correctness.rationale: For compact intrinsic graph with one edge L and m>=2 equally short edges s<=L, the long+one-short circle is isometric: traversing any other arm does not shorten its distances. Mapping each off-circle center to its corresponding point of the selected short edge cannot enlarge distances to the circle; p circle arcs force radius q=(L+s)/(2p). For L>=(p-1)s, exact long-edge centers t_j=(L-(p-1)s)/(2p)+j(L+s)/p cover the entire long edge and all short arms through A or B. For L<(p-1)s, q<s/2; any off-circle center covers <2q of the circle, forcing all p equality centers onto it, but an omitted short-arm midpoint remains distance s/2>q. Compactness yields strictness. This addresses real lengths, all p>=1, equality boundary and all edge interiors. Recomputed independently with exact rational endpoints and obstruction identities; the 344-case/414723-check package log alone was not used as proof.
